name: Alexander Hall
use: First-year-only traditional residence hall, 135 students; Liberal Arts learning community (2nd floor)
builtText: Built 1951; dedicated October 20, 1951 as a men's dormitory

facts.text: Dedicated October 20, 1951 as a men's dormitory and named for Norman Alexander, economics instructor from 1923, Dean of Men 1929-1944 and government department chair.
A first-year-only hall of 135 students with a Liberal Arts learning community on the second floor; it shares an outdoor quad with other halls.

Has a recreation lounge and a separate study lounge, first-floor kitchen and laundry; accessibility features listed are Braille signage, roll-in building access and strobe alerts in some rooms. No air conditioning or elevator is listed.

s19b.title: The Ultimate Ranking of Freshman Dorms at UNH

verdict: Plain 1951 brick dorm with a colonial doorway; no A/C, but students rate it the best first-year hall for its size and location.
notes: No licensed photo found. Archives photo shows a plain three-storey flat-roofed brick block with regular punched windows, a modest postwar dormitory. No renovation history found; 'no AC' inferred from Housing's amenity list, which names AC for halls that have it. Architect unknown. Society19 article metadata says Oct 2025; the 'undecided COLA only' detail may be dated (Housing now says first-year with a Liberal Arts floor).
judgeNotes: Reference photos: modest three-storey Georgian-ish block. Reputation carries it.
